title: More fussing with masks.
description: Mostly longer masks with odd numbers of digits.

notes.body:
added 5 commits
  • e8ee2f4a...0b8acdaf - 4 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • d34d1a1e - More fussing with masks.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3791/diffs?diff_id=222149144&start_sha=e8ee2f4a164dc4f46e68422e08c97b95f4dfa7d6)
Could we ignore the prepending (not required) 0 in the script or this is too complex?

I could ignore 00 bytes at the start of the mask (when reporting that the mask/field is wider than it needs to be).

These checks/changes are pretty marginal, and likely I'm making changes that others might not agree with.  The checks are:

- non-contiguous bits.  There are exceptions (especially when there are multiple reserved bits with fields in-between conflated into one field).  Have probably found only a handful of real bugs this way.

- mask longer than necessary.  This is just checking for leading and trailing 00 bytes.  Of course, if the field is part of e.g. "prot.flags32", it might be good to see all of the related bitfields lining up.  I've seen some cases where it looked like the author just wanted to add a whole header without moving 'offset' along.   Is this the case you were talking about?

- num_digits.  The mask has more hex digits than the width of the field indicates.  These are errors and should be fixed up.  There is also a check for an odd number of digits.  These annoy me when you have e.g. 0x1000000  because you can't tell until you count the zeroes whether the 1 is the 1st or 2nd nibble of a byte.  Might just be me though.

- digits all zeroes.  This annoys me because 0 effectively means no mask.  Maybe we should have used NULL for this, but 0x00000000 means no mask, not a 32-bit mask where none of the bits should be counted.  Again, maybe just me.

I was making reference to the changes gone for packet-pdcp-lte.c or packet-pdcp-nr.c for examples, were you have a 18 bits field. The previous mask was correct as C does not require to have the leading 0 systematically present. I'm not against the change done, but fear that other cases like those ones could be done in never code in the future, leadong to errors with your script.

I agree that the PDCP changes are marginal - I don't want to have to spend a moment deciding if the first byte is 0x3f or 0x03.

CI currently runs ./check_typed_item_calls.py without --mask.  I run it myself sometimes if I have a quiet moment.

It is probably time to make the script differentiate between warnings and errors, and if errors are present, return a non-zero status (and make CI job fail).  Of the mask ones, probably only the one where the mask is wider than the field should be considered an error.

Some of these fussier warnings were written in response to seeing something I didn't like, but after writing it and running on the codebase, I realised there are valid exceptions.  Mostly I pay attention to the detailed warnings for my private dissectors.
